_doc: Site change log. Append a new entry every time we touch a mascot record, swap a photo, change a credit, or add/remove a store. Powers the unified feed on /recent. Newest entries should be at the TOP of the array. Schema: { date (YYYY-MM-DD), kind, store_number?, mascot_id?, summary, reason?, hidden? }. Allowed kinds: 'added' | 'renamed' | 'photo' | 'credit' | 'notes' | 'store_added' | 'store_removed' | 'site'. Set hidden:true on entries you want preserved in this file for audit purposes but suppressed from the public /recent feed (e.g. back-office credit corrections).

events.summary: Map: "Find mascots near me" button — taps the device's GPS to zoom you to your spot
events.reason: Added a red 📍 button anchored to the bottom-right of the main map. Tapping it asks the browser for the user's location (one-time permission prompt), then flies the map to a neighborhood-level zoom (14) with a pulsing blue 'you are here' dot. Errors (permission denied, timeout, unavailable) surface as a 5-second toast above the button. Uses the standard Geolocation API — no extra dependencies, no backend, works the same on desktop Chrome/Safari and mobile. Mobile-first design: full label on tablet/desktop, shortened to 'Near me' on phones so it doesn't crowd the map.

events.summary: Ocho the Octopus joined #252 North Hollywood, CA
events.reason: An octopus in landlocked North Hollywood is itself a small surprise — but the name is a quiet nod to area history. In October 1887, J.B. Lankershim and eight other developers organized the Lankershim Ranch Land and Water Company, the syndicate whose 12,000-acre purchase became modern North Hollywood and the surrounding San Fernando Valley. Ocho (Spanish for 'eight') brings the same number of arms to the job. Photo submitted by David G.

events.summary: Compressed 267 oversize photos (281 MB → 82 MB)
events.reason: DigitalOcean build timed out at the 1-hour wall trying to clone the repo from GitHub. The .git directory was 416 MB and public/photos was 465 MB — including a 13 MB 091.png and dozens of 2–4 MB jpegs that had been committed without compression. Resized everything wider than 1600px and re-encoded at JPEG quality 85; saved ~200 MB of working-tree size. Repo history is still heavy until a future BFG pass, but new clones will be much faster going forward.

events.summary: McQuackers' Quest: lowered minimum-time validation from 30s to 10s
events.reason: Skilled players who know mascot positions can finish all 5 levels in ~15s. A legitimate 0:16 run was being rejected by the Supabase CHECK constraint as 'too fast to be human.' Lowered the floor to 10s in both the client-side score validator and the database constraint; live database was updated directly via an ALTER, and the repo file now matches reality.

Scroll past the first section and McQuackers crashes through the page — then you guide him through 5 real Trader Joe's stores (West Hollywood, Lake Grove, East Liberty Pittsburgh, Silverdale, Rochester) to find their actual cataloged mascots: Steven Sparkles, Schmooli, Tuskanini, Confetti Yeti, Susan Bee Anthony. All art hand-painted via Higgsfield AI in vintage Fearless Flyer style. Time-based scoring, optional hints, global leaderboard with 3-letter initials, brag-share URLs. Also reachable directly at /quack.

events.summary: Database security hardened — RLS gap closed, all advisor warnings resolved
events.reason: Supabase flagged that the submissions and corrections tables had policies but RLS itself was disabled, meaning the policies weren’t being enforced and anyone with the public anon key could read or modify those tables. Enabled RLS on both, then went on to clear every other security advisory: REVOKE'd REST execute on the two trigger functions, pinned a search_path on touch_updated_at, dropped the broad listing policy on the mascot-photos bucket, and tightened the three public-facing INSERT policies with size caps and forced pending-status. Site is now clean on Supabase’s security linter (zero findings).
